answer: Attention Ledger Admission. Each identity must hold a publicly logged stream of short, randomly scheduled check-ins; missed windows decay its score. A beacon slot is granted only when recent check-in density clears a threshold. The atlas of active scores is public, so duplicates are visible but not disqualifying; what matters is the river of continuous presence each one must sustain. An attacker running N identities pays N times the scheduled attention and cannot batch or defer it, since windows are unpredictable and non-transferable.
